extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, patent agent applicants, and USPTO/OED staff
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, legal bases, and sanctioning criteria applied by the USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline when a registered patent practitioner (or applicant) makes false statements on a registration application or otherwise engages in misconduct; includes reinstatement conditions and publication/administrative procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO jurisdiction over disciplinary matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceedings against practitioners are brought under these statutory authorities; disciplinary actions should be grounded in these provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered practitioners subject to USPTO professional rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent ... has been a registered practitioner (Registration No. 67,701) and subject to the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility set forth at 37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq. and the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct set forth at 37 C.F.R. § 11.101 et seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All registered practitioners must comply with the cited Code and Rules; violations of those rules can form the basis for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truthfulness in registration application (37 C.F.R. § 10.22(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Making a false statement in connection with registration violates 37 C.F.R. § 10.22(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: False answers on the Application for Registration to Practice before the USPTO (including questions about prior charges, discipline, termination, or resignations while under investigation) constitute grounds for disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material registration questions must be answered accurately (questions 15,18,19,20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Application questions at issue include: (15) 'Have any charges ever been preferred against you in connection with your practice...?', (18) 'Have you ever been disciplined, reprimanded, or suspended in any job for conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, misrepresentation, deceit, or any violation of Federal or State laws or regulations?', (19) 'Have you ever been fired or discharged from any job, or have been asked to resign or quit for conduct involving dishonesty...?', (20) 'Have you ever resigned or quit a job when you were under investigation or inquiry for conduct which could have been considered as involving dishonesty...?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must answer these and similar questions truthfully; affirmative histories must be disclosed even if court jurisdiction was later terminated.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED reliance on application representations
rubrics_metrics.description: OED relied on the information and representations contained in the Application, and granted Respondent patent agent status on or about January 19, 2011.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Misrepresentations on an application are significant because OED's grant of registration is predicated on those representations; undisclosed adverse facts can invalidate that reliance and lead to discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction: suspension period
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is hereby suspended from practice before the USPTO in patent, trademark and other non-patent matters for eighteen (18) months commencing on the date a Final Order approving this Agreement is signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension is a primary sanction for false statements in a registration application; the duration specified here is 18 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension remains until petitioned reinstatement (37 C.F.R. § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall remain suspended from practice before the Office ... until the OED Director grants a petition reinstating Respondent pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A suspended practitioner must follow the petition-for-reinstatement process in § 11.60; suspension does not automatically end after the period unless reinstatement requirements are satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement additional conditions: MPRE and demonstration of fitness
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director's granting of any petition for reinstatement ... is additionally predicated upon Respondent retaking and passing the Multistate Professional Responsibility Examination, obtaining a scaled score equal to or greater than 85 and presenting the results to OED, and demonstrating good moral character, reputation, competency, and learning in the law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement may require passing the MPRE to a specified score (>=85) and affirmative demonstration of character and competence; meeting statutory petition procedures alone may be insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 (attorney/practitioner duties)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspended practitioners must comply with the obligations set out in § 11.58 (e.g., duties upon suspension or resignation); noncompliance can be independently actionable.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office must follow the procedural and publication duties specified in § 11.59 when imposing discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on obtaining a USPTO Customer Number while suspended
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for or obtain a USPTO Customer Number unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners under suspension are barred from registering for customer numbers that would enable practice before the Office until reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at the OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room ... The OED Director publish a notice in the Official Gazette that is materially consistent with the following: [Notice of Suspension text].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary actions will be made public via OED's FOIA Reading Room and an Official Gazette notice; the notice typically summarizes the misconduct, sanction, and reinstatement conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this Agreement or the Final Order shall prevent the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding ...: (1) when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct ...; (2) in any future disciplinary proceeding against Respondent (i) as an aggravating factor ... and/or (ii) to rebut any statement or representation by or on Respondent's behalf;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior discipline may be treated as aggravating or evidentiary in subsequent complaints or proceedings; settlement does not shield a practitioner from future consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative procedural action: motion to dismiss pending proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall file a motion with the administrative law judge requesting the dismissal of the pending disciplinary proceeding within fourteen (14) days of the date of the Final Order;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a settlement resolves matters, OED will take administrative steps (e.g., move to dismiss related pending proceedings) within specified timeframes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs in settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this Agreement and the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The settlement sets cost responsibility—here, each party bears its own costs; this is an explicit settlement term to note.
